questions.text: Consider the following snapshot of a system running n concurrent processes. Process [latex]i[/latex] is holding [latex]X_i[/latex] instances of a resource R, [latex] 1\leq i\leq n[/latex]. Assume that all instances of R are currently in use. Further, for all [latex]i[/latex], process [latex]i[/latex] can place a request for at most [latex]Y_i[/latex] additional instances of R while holding the [latex]X_i[/latex] instances it already has. Of the n processes, there are exactly two processes p and q such that [latex]Y_p=Y_q=0[/latex]. Which one of the following conditions guarantees that no other process apart from p and q can complete execution?
questions.solution:
p and q need nothing more, so they finish and release [latex]X_p+X_q[/latex] instances (all others are in use).

Any other process k can finish only if it gets [latex]Y_k[/latex] instances. If [latex]X_p+X_q \lt \min_k Y_k[/latex], the freed instances are not enough for any other process, so none of them can complete.

Answer: [latex]X_p+X_q \lt Min\{Y_k\}[/latex]

questions.text: Assume that in a certain computer, the virtual addresses are 64 bits long and the physical addresses are 48 bits long. The memory is word addressable. The page size is 8kB and the word size is 4 bytes. The Translation Look-aside Buffer (TLB) in the address translation path has 128 valid entries. At most how many distinct virtual addresses can be translated without any TLB miss?
questions.solution:
Word addressable, word = 4 bytes, so one page = 8 KB / 4 B = [latex]2^{11}[/latex] words = 2048 addresses.

128 TLB entries cover 128 pages: [latex]128\times2^{11}=2^{18}=256\times2^{10}[/latex] addresses without a TLB miss.

Answer: [latex]256\times2^{10}[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider three concurrent processes P1, P2 and P3 as shown below, which access a shared variable D that has been initialized to 100.

The process are executed on a uniprocessor system running a time-shared operating system. If the minimum and maximum possible values of D after the three processes have completed execution are X and Y respectively, then the value of Y-X is __________.
questions.solution:
Each update is really load D, change, store D, so a process can overwrite the others' results.

- Maximum: lose P2's update. P1 reads 100; P2 runs fully (D = 50); P1 writes 120; then P3 makes it 130. So [latex]Y=130[/latex].
- Minimum: lose both additions. P2 reads 100; P1 and P3 run fully (D = 130); P2 writes 100 [latex]-[/latex] 50 = 50. So [latex]X=50[/latex].

[latex]Y-X=130-50=80[/latex]

Answer: 80

fork() is called when i is even: i = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 times, and every existing process forks each time.

Total processes [latex]=2^5=32[/latex]; one is the original, so children [latex]=32-1=31[/latex].

Answer: 31

questions.text:
In multi-programmed systems, it is advantageous if some programs such as editors and compilers can be shared by several users.
Which of the following must be true of multi-programmed systems in order that a single copy of a program can be shared by several users?

I. The program is a macro
II. The program is recursive
III. The program is reentrant
questions.solution:
One copy of code can be shared by many users only if it is reentrant: it never modifies itself and keeps per-user data separate (on each user's stack or data area).

Answer: III only
